x-m-e5-03.title: Finding Wrong Answers Without Calculating
x-m-e5-03.goal: Estimate the size of a fraction-addition answer to rule out wrong answers, then find several fraction pairs wey make same total.
x-m-e5-03.material: Four friends calculate 2/3 + 1/4. Seonu say 3/7, Bora say 5/6, Sian say 1 5/12, and Doyun say 11/12. See whether you fit rule out wrong answers with estimate alone before calculating.

x-m-e5-03.thinking.1: Telling apart wetin estimate fit tell you and wetin e no fit tell you
x-m-e5-03.thinking.2: Finding several pairs wey make same total
x-m-e5-03.prereq.0: How to compare fractions with different denominators (Grade 5, first semester level)
x-m-e5-03.s.s1.prompt: Choose all the answers you fit call "wrong" using only these two estimates: "the total bigger than 2/3" and "the total smaller than 1," without exact calculation.
x-m-e5-03.s.s1.hint.0: If you add positive number to 2/3, the answer go bigger or smaller than 2/3?
x-m-e5-03.s.s1.hint.1: Compare the number you add, 1/4, with 1/3, then think whether total go pass or fall short of 1.
x-m-e5-03.s.s1.r.a: This consider say answer no fit be smaller than starting number 2/3.
x-m-e5-03.s.s1.r.b: 5/6 bigger than 2/3 and smaller than 1, so these two estimates no fit show say e wrong. Estimation fit filter wrong answers, but no confirm say the remaining ones correct.
x-m-e5-03.s.s1.r.c: This use the fact say 1/4 smaller than 1/3 to think total must be smaller than 1.
x-m-e5-03.s.s1.r.d: This number dey between 2/3 and 1, so estimation no rule am out. To choose from remaining options, you need exact calculation.
x-m-e5-03.s.s1.explain: We add 1/4 to 2/3, so total must bigger than 2/3. So 3/7 (about 0.43) no work. Also, 1/4 smaller than 1/3, so total must be smaller than 2/3 plus 1/3, which na 1. So 1 and 5/12 no work too. 5/6 and 11/12 dey between 2/3 and 1, so these estimates no rule dem out (the actual answer na one of the two).
x-m-e5-03.s.s2.prompt: Make 2 different pairs of proper fractions with different denominators, wey no fit simplify again (numerators a and c, denominators b and d, denominators 12 or less), and total na 11/12.
x-m-e5-03.s.s2.hint.0: First write pairs where, after changing denominators to 12, some/12 + some/12 = 11/12.
x-m-e5-03.s.s2.hint.1: Check whether the pairs you write can change to forms wey no fraction fit simplify and denominators different.
x-m-e5-03.s.s2.fail.c1: Numerator must be 1 or more and smaller than denominator.
x-m-e5-03.s.s2.ok.c2: All numbers natural numbers, and denominators no pass 12.
x-m-e5-03.s.s2.fail.c2: Make all numbers natural and denominators no pass 12.
x-m-e5-03.s.s2.fail.c4: The two denominators na the same. Make dem different.
x-m-e5-03.s.s2.ok.c5: The total of the two fractions na 11/12.
x-m-e5-03.s.s2.fail.c5: The total of the two fractions no be 11/12.
x-m-e5-03.s.s2.explain: For example, 2/3+1/4, 1/2+5/12, 1/3+7/12, 1/6+3/4, and 1/12+5/6 all make 11/12. The same pair in reverse order (for example, 1/4+2/3) count as same example.
x-m-e5-03.s.s3.prompt: Seonu talk, "Just add the denominators and numerators together," and get 2/3+1/4=3/7. Explain to Seonu (1) why e wrong using estimate, without calculating, and (2) correct calculation method with common denominators.
x-m-e5-03.s.s3.hint.0: Compare Seonu answer 3/7 with starting number 2/3 using decimal or 0.5, then see which bigger.
x-m-e5-03.s.s3.hint.1: Find number wey both denominators 3 and 4 fit divide evenly, then change both fractions to same denominator.
x-m-e5-03.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Your estimate show why Seonu answer 3/7 impossible?
x-m-e5-03.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Clear say for common-denominator calculation you only add numerators?
x-m-e5-03.s.s3.model.0: Seonu, if you add 1/4 to 2/3, answer suppose pass 2/3, but 3/7 smaller than 2/3, so e wrong. When denominators different, change both to common denominator 12 and add 8/12+3/12=11/12.
x-m-e5-03.s.s3.model.1: 3/7 smaller than 0.5, but 2/3 bigger than 0.5, so adding no fit make answer smaller. No add denominators. Make common denominator 12, a common multiple of 3 and 4, then add only numerators.

x-m-e5-10.s.s1.explain: Each time you add a square, matchsticks increase by 3. First square get 4, and each time one join, add 3, so with n squares e be 3×n+1.

x-m-e5-01.title: Finding Two Numbers with Given Greatest Common Factor and Least Common Multiple
x-m-e5-01.goal: Find two numbers yourself wey meet GCF and LCM conditions together, and find relationship between conditions.
x-m-e5-01.material: Seoa draw two number cards. Both numbers natural and no pass 40. Seoa only say: "Greatest common factor of both numbers na 6, and least common multiple na 36." What both numbers be? (Say smaller one first.)
x-m-e5-01.thinking.0: Read conditions as relationship between factors and multiples
x-m-e5-01.thinking.1: Find and check examples wey meet all conditions
x-m-e5-01.thinking.2: Guess pattern from examples you find
x-m-e5-01.prereq.0: Meaning of factor, multiple, common factor and common multiple (Grade 5, first semester)
x-m-e5-01.s.s1.prompt: From statement GCF of two numbers na 6, wetin must be true about both numbers?
x-m-e5-01.s.s1.hint.0: Turn "both numbers get 6 as factor" into statement about dividing both numbers by 6.
x-m-e5-01.s.s1.hint.1: Write some numbers wey connect to 6, like 6, 12, 18, 24, and check whether 6 factor or multiple of dem.
x-m-e5-01.s.s1.r.a: You understand "common divisor" as "number wey divide both without remainder" and think about the connection between divisors and multiples.
x-m-e5-01.s.s1.r.b: The only divisors of 6 na 1, 2, 3, and 6. Think whether the two numbers fit bigger than 6.
x-m-e5-01.s.s1.o.c: At least one of the two numbers na 6.
x-m-e5-01.s.s1.r.c: Even if greatest common factor na 6, both numbers fit bigger than 6. Test using two multiples of 6 wey bigger than 6.
x-m-e5-01.s.s1.o.d: The difference between the two numbers na 6.
x-m-e5-01.s.s1.r.d: Choose two multiples of 6 and compare their greatest common factor with their difference. Dem always the same?
x-m-e5-01.s.s1.explain: 6 na common factor of the two numbers, so both numbers divide evenly by 6. That mean both na multiples of 6. The extra condition say greatest common factor no pass 6 when both multiples of 6 fit be tested in next step.
x-m-e5-01.s.s2.prompt: Find 2 different pairs of numbers wey follow the conditions (smaller number a, bigger number b). The bigger number no pass 40.
x-m-e5-01.s.s2.hint.0: Both numbers na multiples of 6, so each fit write as 6 times one natural number. First write all multiples of 6 up to 40.
x-m-e5-01.s.s2.hint.1: Pair two of dem and check whether least common multiple na 36 and greatest common factor no pass 6. If no, choose different pair.
x-m-e5-01.s.s2.fail.c1: Both numbers must be natural numbers.
x-m-e5-01.s.s2.ok.c2: Smaller number less than bigger number, and bigger number no pass 40.
x-m-e5-01.s.s2.fail.c2: Write smaller number as a and bigger number as b, and make b no pass 40.
x-m-e5-01.s.s2.fail.c3: The greatest common factor of the two numbers no be 6.
x-m-e5-01.s.s2.fail.c4: The least common multiple of the two numbers no be 36.
x-m-e5-01.s.s2.explain: (12, 18) and (6, 36) na all the pairs wey follow the conditions. For 12=6×2 and 18=6×3, when you divide both numbers by 6, 2 and 3 no get any common factor except 1, and 6×2×3=36. 6=6×1 and 36=6×6 work the same way.
x-m-e5-01.s.s3.prompt: For each of the two pairs you find, calculate the product of both numbers. How the products come out? Na coincidence? Compare with product of greatest common factor 6 and least common multiple 36 too, then write your guess.
x-m-e5-01.s.s3.hint.0: For each pair you find first, multiply the two numbers and write the answer.
x-m-e5-01.s.s3.hint.1: Find the product of 6 and 36 too, put am beside the products above and compare.
x-m-e5-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You calculate again to check say the products for both pairs really the same?
x-m-e5-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You test your idea about 'Na coincidence?' with two other numbers too (for example, 4 and 6)?
x-m-e5-01.s.s3.model.0: 12×18=216 and 6×36=216, so the two pair products na the same. Greatest common factor 6 times least common multiple 36 na 216 too, so e no look like coincidence.
x-m-e5-01.s.s3.model.1: When you calculate, 12×18 na 216 and 6×36 na 216. The product of two numbers look like e always equal (greatest common factor)×(least common multiple). When I test 4 and 6, 2×12=24=4×6, so e work.
x-m-e5-01.s.s3.modelNote.1: An answer wey even test with other numbers
x-m-e5-01.s.s3.model.2: So I think say product of two numbers always equal product of GCD and LCM. 12×18 na 216, and 6×36 na 216 too.
